content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To knit a blanket, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sketch the blanket design and dimensions (1 hour)
Step 2. Research different wool blends for warmth (2 hours)
Step 3. Choose a decorative border pattern (30 minutes)
Step 4. Finalize the tension square measurements (20 minutes)
Step 5. Wind the first five hanks into balls (1 hour)
Step 6. Practice the cabling technique on a swatch (2 hours)
Step 7. Calculate the total yardage required (15 minutes)
Step 8. Print out the full-size knitting chart (10 minutes)
Step 9. Organize the yarn by color gradient (45 minutes)
Step 10. Purchase a set of high-quality bamboo needles (1 hour)
Step 11. Cast on the foundation row (40 minutes)
Step 12. Determine the number of stitches for the width (15 minutes)
Step 13. Select the primary color palette (1 hour)
Step 14. Order the bulk yarn from a supplier (30 minutes)
Step 15. Knit the final finishing edge (5 hours)
Step 16. Weave in all loose ends with a tapestry needle (3 hours)
Step 17. Watch a tutorial on the "seed stitch" (20 minutes)
Step 18. Knit the main body of the blanket (40 hours)
Step 19. Steam block the finished fabric to set shape (24 hours)
Step 20. Check the dye lot numbers on all skeins (10 minutes)
Step 21. Set up a comfortable knitting station with lighting (1 hour)
Step 22. Clear a large workspace for assembly (30 minutes)
Step 23. Attach a handmade "Care Instructions" label (15 minutes)
Step 24. Unpack the shipping boxes (20 minutes)
Step 25. Sort the circular needles by size (15 minutes)
Step 26. Create a progress tracking sheet (15 minutes)
Step 27. Test the yarn for colorfastness (12 hours)
Step 28. Wash the raw wool if necessary (3 hours)
Step 29. Decide on the blanket's recipient (5 minutes)
Step 30. Browse inspiration photos online (2 hours)
Step 31. Knit the first ten rows of the pattern (4 hours)
Step 32. Select a matching thread for the lining (30 minutes)
Step 33. Join the first and second balls of yarn (10 minutes)
Step 34. Knit the middle section panels (30 hours)
Step 35. Read through the entire pattern instructions (1 hour)
Step 36. Measure the width of the initial rows (5 minutes)
Step 37. Buy a fabric backing for extra weight (2 hours)
Step 38. Knit the intricate lace border (15 hours)
Step 39. Measure the available storage space for the project (10 minutes)
Step 40. Prepare the stitch markers (10 minutes)
Step 41. Photograph the yarn for a project blog (20 minutes)
Step 42. Verify the needle gauge size (5 minutes)
Step 43. Double-check the row count (10 minutes)
Step 44. Correct any dropped stitches in the early rows (30 minutes)
Step 45. Bind off the last row of stitches (1 hour)
Step 46. Calculate the weight of the completed piece (10 minutes)
Step 47. Read reviews of the yarn texture (1 hour)
Step 48. Purchase a large project bag (45 minutes)
Step 49. Wind the remaining yarn hanks (2 hours)
Step 50. Cut the fabric backing to size (1 hour)
Step 51. Place markers at every twenty-stitch interval (30 minutes)
Step 52. Sharpen the tips of the wooden needles (15 minutes)
Step 53. Sanitize the knitting area (30 minutes)
Step 54. Compare prices at different craft stores (2 hours)
Step 55. Set a completion deadline on the calendar (10 minutes)
Step 56. Learn how to do a Russian Join (30 minutes)
Step 57. Adjust the chair height for ergonomics (5 minutes)
Step 58. Clean the knitting needles (10 minutes)
Step 59. Invite a friend for a knitting circle (15 minutes)
Step 60. Pre-wash the fabric backing (2 hours)
Step 61. Inspect the yarn for any factory knots (1 hour)
Step 62. Wrap the blanket in tissue paper for storage (15 minutes)
Step 63. Knit a small sample swatch (2 hours)
Step 64. Count the number of skeins available (5 minutes)
Step 65. Weigh the leftover yarn (10 minutes)
Step 66. Check for any inconsistencies in yarn thickness (1 hour)
Step 67. Apply a fabric protector spray (4 hours)
Step 68. Sign up for a knitting technique newsletter (5 minutes)
Step 69. Set a budget for the project (15 minutes)
Step 70. Find a crochet hook for fixing errors (10 minutes)
